fencer.name: Аполлон
fencer.intro: Learn how to counter Apollo in Deadlock. Compare items for his mobility and spirit burst, bait Riposte, and plan your response to his ultimate.
role_text: Threaten a burst window, then use defensive timing and movement to survive the response.
**How to disrupt it:** Draw out Riposte or movement before committing your decisive damage.
glance: Apollo is hard to punish when Riposte and his movement are both available.
Give him a small attack to react to, then commit once the defensive response is spent.
Grounding him creates a finish window; spirit defense helps if you are dying before you can use it.
fencer.note: Fit the counter into your own build. Choose one answer to the immediate problem, check what teammates already provide, and keep enough damage to use the opening.

problems.problem: Apollo mobility and Flawless Advance keep letting him escape
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Consider Slowing Hex when fighting Apollo if Flawless Advance lets him escape your damage. Buy it when denying that movement would create a kill window your team can use.
problems.how: Use Slowing Hex before Apollo starts Flawless Advance, then focus him while that escape is unavailable. If he cleanses the effect, hold another control source for his next escape rather than assuming the first hex will secure the kill.

problems.problem: His spirit burst is deleting you before you can trade back
problems.label: Larger investment
problems.when: Buy Spellbreaker if Apollo is taking too much of your health with his front-loaded spirit combo. Choose it when a large opening spirit hit is the part that makes the fight unwinnable.
problems.how: Choose it when a large spirit-damage hit is the reason you die before responding. Its conditional protection has a cooldown and does not negate every part of the combo.

problems.problem: Apollo’s ultimate keeps finishing you after the setup
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Consider Counterspell against Apollo when the damaging part of his ultimate keeps deciding the fight and you can reliably read the timing. Choose a steadier defensive answer if that reaction is not dependable.
problems.how: Time the spell parry for the actual damage, rather than the first setup cue. Apollo can delay his commitment until your protection ends.

problems.problem: Apollo cleanses Slowing Hex and escapes anyway
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Buy Silence Wave when Apollo keeps getting a key ability or defensive response off before your team can finish the fight. Your team needs damage ready during the denial window.
problems.how: A follow-up when he cleanses movement denial or must not cast another escape. Coordinate allied damage during the silence window.

problems.problem: Apollo’s spirit damage is forcing you out of fights
problems.label: Larger investment
problems.when: Buy Spirit Resilience if Apollo is taking too much of your health with his front-loaded spirit combo. Prioritize it when that damage keeps forcing you to retreat across several exchanges.
problems.how: Use for recurring spirit damage across several exchanges, especially when you cannot depend on one timed defensive response. It does not stop his movement.

problems.problem: Apollo keeps escaping or denying your finish
problems.label: Larger investment
problems.when: Buy Cursed Relic when Apollo keeps getting a key ability or defensive response off before your team can finish the fight. Your team needs damage ready during the denial window.
problems.how: A larger team utility investment when silence, disarm and item denial are needed together. Use when allies can finish him; account for the item's outgoing-damage penalty.

problems.problem: His spell trade is winning before you can punish the escape
problems.label: Early / mid-game option
problems.when: Consider Spirit Sap when Apollo’s Spirit-scaling damage is deciding trades and your team can return spirit damage.
problems.how: Apply before the spell exchange, then follow up together. Respect Riposte and save a response for his movement; Spirit Sap neither denies the escape nor protects you from every part of his combo.

Trade after the defensive cooldown is spent, and keep stamina for his return engage.
**When terrain allows, a tighter route limits the distance his movement can create.** Avoid following him into an unsupported chase.
An early Slowing Hex is useful when mobility is denying your lane’s kill attempts.
fight: **Land movement denial when allies can immediately follow up.** If he cleanses the first application, hold a second control source for the escape.
When he commits his ultimate in open space, move toward your team or your side of the map so the commitment leaves him exposed.
**Time Counterspell for the damaging part of the ultimate.** Activating it at the first sign of the setup gives him room to delay.
If the same burst keeps killing you through good positioning, invest in spirit defense rather than adding another chase item.
faq: What is Apollo’s biggest weakness?

Apollo becomes easier to punish after Riposte or his movement is spent. Test the defensive response with a low-risk attack, then commit when he cannot freely answer or escape. Slowing Hex is valuable when denying Flawless Advance gives your team an immediate finish window.
What should you buy first against Apollo in lane?

Slowing Hex is the lane option when Apollo’s movement keeps denying kill attempts. Apply it before his movement sequence and have damage ready. Test Riposte with gunfire or a small commitment first; spending your strongest ability into his defensive response can waste the opening before the hex matters.
Which counter items matter against Apollo later in the game?

Choose Spirit Resilience for repeated spirit damage or Spellbreaker when Apollo’s opening burst decides the exchange. Add coordinated cast denial if he cleanses your movement lock and escapes. Silence Wave or Cursed Relic needs allied damage ready; buying more control without follow-up may only delay the reset.
Should you buy bullet or spirit resistance against Apollo?

Spirit protection is the more relevant defense when Apollo’s front-loaded combo is taking your health. Spirit Resilience works across repeated exchanges, while Spellbreaker addresses a large conditional burst hit. These purchases help you survive; movement denial and coordinated damage are still needed to stop Flawless Advance from rescuing him.
How do you respond to Apollo’s ultimate?

Counterspell answers the damaging part of Apollo’s ultimate when you can read the timing. Save it for the actual hit rather than the earliest setup cue. Apollo can delay his commitment, so an early activation may end before the damage arrives. Spirit defense is steadier when that reaction is unreliable.
Do anti-heal items work against Apollo?

Anti-heal is only a priority against Apollo when healing or lifesteal is actually preventing your team’s finish. Use Slowing Hex before Apollo starts Flawless Advance, then focus him while that escape is unavailable.
What can you cleanse or remove in the Apollo matchup?

The Apollo plan uses timed protection and movement denial rather than treating Dispel Magic as an ultimate cleanse. Save Counterspell for the damage window. If Apollo cleanses your Slowing Hex, layer another control source or Silence Wave during a commitment your team can punish.
What positioning mistakes should you avoid against Apollo?

Test Riposte with gunfire or a low-risk attack instead of opening with your strongest ability. Trade after the defensive cooldown is spent, and keep stamina for his return engage. Land movement denial when allies can immediately follow up.

baba.name: Буся
baba.intro: Counter Baba in Deadlock with spirit defense, Dispel Magic, and control protection. Learn how to answer Threadsap, Brew silence, and her pigeon transformation.
role_text: Use spell pressure and transformation windows to contest space; empowered shooting changes the damage mix.
**How to disrupt it:** Respect her transformation, change the fighting angle, and pressure once that window ends.
glance: Baba can win with empowered shooting, Granny Long Legs, or a teamfight ultimate, so identify which part is deciding the exchange.
Respect the transformation, then pressure after she spends it.
Spirit defense, a reliable parry and a planned ultimate response are more useful than buying every possible counter.
baba.note: Fit the counter into your own build. Choose one answer to the immediate problem, check what teammates already provide, and keep enough damage to use the opening.

problems.problem: Threadsap or Brew debuffs are ruining my trades
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Buy Dispel Magic if Baba keeps making trades or escapes unsafe with Threadsap or Brew debuffs. It fits when clearing that effect would let you reposition or fight back; it is not a purchase for raw damage alone.
problems.how: Buy when those effects repeatedly cost you a trade or prevent your response. Use after the important debuff lands. It does not cleanse her ultimate transformation.

problems.problem: Repeated spirit damage wears me down
problems.label: Larger investment
problems.when: Buy Spirit Resilience if Baba is taking too much of your health with Threadsap, Brew and Feed the Birds. Prioritize it when that damage keeps forcing you to retreat across several exchanges.
problems.how: Choose it when recurring spirit damage is the main problem. Damage resistance does not prevent silence or pigeon transformation.

problems.problem: Granny Long Legs wins every close-range exchange
problems.label: Lane option
problems.when: Buy Rebuttal when Baba keeps winning close trades with parryable melee pressure and you can consistently read the hit. It rewards that response; it does not replace learning the timing.
problems.how: Buy early when kicks and ground slams repeatedly force you out of lane and you can time your parry. Parrying her kick stuns Baba; parrying the ground slam blocks the hit without stunning her.

problems.problem: Feed the Birds keeps deciding the teamfight
problems.label: Larger investment
problems.when: Consider Cursed Relic when Baba gets uncontested Feed the Birds channels and your team can punish her during an interrupt window. Check for control immunity before depending on it.
problems.how: Use during the channel while your team can follow up. It also strips eligible non-ultimate buffs. It lowers your outgoing damage; Unstoppable can block it. Use cover when immunity prevents the interrupt.

problems.problem: Threadsap-enhanced shooting is the main threat
problems.label: Larger investment
problems.when: Buy Plated Armor when you notice that Baba is winning because her Threadsap-enhanced shooting wins the exchange. It is an option when weapon pressure keeps wearing you down across fights.
problems.how: Buy when Baba’s empowered bullets are a major threat. Its protection is chance-based, so avoid relying on it to guarantee a safe trade.

problems.problem: Feed the Birds’ final hit keeps transforming you
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Consider Counterspell against Baba when Feed the Birds’ final hit keeps deciding the fight and you can reliably read the timing. Choose a steadier defensive answer if that reaction is not dependable.
problems.how: Save the spell parry for Feed the Birds’ final hit. Earlier bread effects and the final hit are separate timing windows; activating too early can leave the transformation unanswered.

problems.problem: Healing keeps her alive through focused damage
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Buy Decay when Baba’s healing or lifesteal is preventing your team from finishing a focused target. Consider it when you need a targeted anti-heal response without building up weapon hits.
problems.how: Buy when healing items or upgraded melee lifesteal keep Baba alive. It can be cleansed and does not reduce Soothing Brew’s barrier.

problems.problem: Baba stays effective because your team cannot interrupt the commitment
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Buy Knockdown if Baba keeps getting uncontested value from Feed the Birds and your team lacks a reliable stop. Coordinate damage for the delayed stun rather than buying it without a follow-up plan.
problems.how: Cast early enough for the stun to land during the channel. Baba can release early or protect herself with immunity. Treat a shorter channel as pressure, not a guaranteed cancel.

problems.problem: Baba’s committed burst leaves you no safe escape
problems.label: Situational response
problems.when: Consider Ethereal Shift if Baba’s Feed the Birds’ final hit is killing you before you can reach cover. You need time to activate it before control removes your response.
problems.how: Use before the final damage and transformation arrive. Duration upgrades can outlast your protection. Have cover or follow-up ready when you return.

problems.problem: Her Spirit-scaling pressure is winning repeated trades
problems.label: Early / mid-game option
problems.when: Consider Spirit Sap when Threadsap-enhanced pressure or another Spirit-scaling part of Baba’s build is deciding the exchange.
problems.how: Target Baba before the trade and return spirit damage while she is affected. It does not cleanse Threadsap, disarm her or stop Granny Long Legs; choose a separate answer when melee pressure or control is the main threat.

Rebuttal supports repeated parry opportunities; recovery or early spirit protection helps if spell damage is costing you farm.
fight: Spread around objectives and break Feed the Birds' line of sight before the channel builds value on the whole team.
**Coordinate a vulnerable-channel interrupt.** Knockdown must land before the channel ends, and Baba can release early or use immunity.
If you cannot leave, save Counterspell's spell parry or Ethereal Shift for the decisive final hit, with a plan for when protection ends.
**Pressure after Granny Long Legs ends rather than spending every disable into its debuff resistance.** Choose anti-heal for lifesteal or healing items, not Soothing Brew's barrier.
faq: What is Baba’s biggest weakness?

Baba is more punishable after she spends the tool that is winning the exchange. Identify empowered shooting, Granny Long Legs or Feed the Birds first, then respond to that threat. Parrying a readable kick creates a window, while breaking the ultimate’s line of sight denies easy teamwide value.
What should you buy first against Baba in lane?

Rebuttal fits Baba’s repeated kicks and ground slams when you can read the parry. Dispel Magic is relevant when Threadsap or Brew debuffs prevent a useful return trade. Take cover after Threadsap instead of forcing a weakened spell combo into empowered gunfire; the item should support that reset.
Which counter items matter against Baba later in the game?

Build Spirit Resilience for recurring spirit damage, or Plated Armor when empowered bullets are the main threat. For Feed the Birds, prepare an interrupt or a timed defensive response rather than buying every option. Decay is conditional on healing items or upgraded melee lifesteal keeping Baba alive.
Should you buy bullet or spirit resistance against Baba?

Choose spirit defense when Baba’s abilities and Feed the Birds are taking most of your health; consider Plated Armor when Threadsap-enhanced shooting wins the trade. Resistance does not prevent every control effect or the ultimate transformation. Check the actual damage source before committing to a larger defense.
How do you respond to Baba’s Feed The Birds?

Knockdown or Cursed Relic can pressure a vulnerable Feed the Birds channel; Counterspell or Ethereal Shift can answer the final dangerous hit. Cast an interrupt early enough to land, and account for control immunity or an early release. The final transformation has a separate timing window from earlier effects.
Do anti-heal items work against Baba?

Yes, when Baba’s healing items or upgraded melee lifesteal keep her alive through focused damage. Decay can reduce that recovery, but it does not shrink Soothing Brew’s barrier or prevent the ultimate transformation. Identify the threat first so anti-heal does not replace the parry, spirit defense or ultimate response you need.
What can you cleanse or remove in the Baba matchup?

Dispel Magic can remove eligible Threadsap or Brew debuffs, but it does not cleanse Baba’s ultimate transformation. Clear the important debuff after it lands, then move to cover or a better angle. Plan an interrupt or timed protection for Feed the Birds instead of expecting one cleanse to answer both threats.
What positioning mistakes should you avoid against Baba?

Take cover after Threadsap lands rather than forcing a weakened spell combo into her empowered shots. Parry Granny Long Legs when you can read the attack. The kick stuns Baba when parried; the ground slam can be blocked without stunning her.

deadpack.name: Дохлый Дэнни
deadpack.intro: Counter Deadman Danny in Deadlock with anti-air, spirit defense and safer positioning. Find items for Strix Salvo, Jettison Fuel and Close The Deal.
role_text: Pressure from an aerial angle, mark a target, then commit a dive or grab when the finish is available.
**How to disrupt it:** Use overhead cover, deny the next cast and punish an exposed landing with teammates ready.
glance: Deadman Danny combines aerial angles with marked-target burst and a close-range grab. Keep cover above you, leave missile lines early, and make him commit his landing away from your team. Spirit defense answers much of his ability damage; fuel spray and bullet-resistance reduction create a separate weapon threat.
Deny the aerial angle and punish a missed landing while his movement is unavailable.
Start with the damage or catch costing you fights, then add a coordinated anti-air or cast-denial response.
deadpack.note: Fit the counter into your own build. Choose one answer to the immediate problem, check what teammates already provide, and keep enough damage to use the opening.

problems.problem: Strix Salvo follow-up keeps forcing you out of lane
problems.label: Lane
problems.when: Buy Spirit Shielding when repeated spirit follow-up leaves you too low to keep farming. It is a smaller lane investment before committing to sustained spirit resistance.
problems.how: Its triggered barrier helps absorb follow-up spirit pressure after a qualifying hit. It does not remove a mark or replace stepping out of the missile line.

problems.problem: His landing stun leads to lethal follow-up
problems.label: Lane
problems.when: Choose Reactive Barrier when a landing stun repeatedly turns into a losing lane trade. Buy for the damage after the catch rather than expecting it to prevent the engage.
problems.how: An automatic barrier can cushion follow-up after qualifying control. It does not stop Close The Deal from grabbing you or move you away from the landing.

problems.problem: You run out of movement before his missiles or landing arrive
problems.label: Lane
problems.when: Buy Extra Stamina when you regularly spend your movement before Danny commits his missile line, fuel spray or landing. Keep the extra dash available for that threat.
problems.how: Another movement option helps you leave a delayed missile line or change angle before a dive connects. It is useful before you lose your actions, not an escape button during the grab.

problems.problem: He keeps shooting safely from the air
problems.label: Mid Game
problems.when: Buy Knockdown when Danny’s exposed aerial position lets him deal damage without a team response. Your allies should be close enough to use the delayed catch.
problems.how: The delayed stun gives your team a control window against an exposed airborne target. Cast before the dangerous commit and check his protection; it is not an instant answer once you have already been grabbed.

problems.problem: Missile burst and the ultimate take too much of your health
problems.label: Mid Game
problems.when: Build Spirit Resilience when Strix Salvo, landing explosions or Close The Deal repeatedly force you out of fights. Choose it for recurring spirit damage across several exchanges.
problems.how: Passive spirit protection reduces the damage side of his ability pressure, including the spirit-damage ultimate. It does not prevent the grab, shorten the flight sequence or protect against the weapon-damage fuel spray.

problems.problem: He gets another dive or grab off before you can finish him
problems.label: Mid Game
problems.when: Buy Silence Wave when your team can focus Danny but his next ability keeps extending the fight. Use the denial window with allied damage ready.
problems.how: Land it before the cast you want to deny. It helps create a finish window; do not assume silence cancels Close The Deal after a target has already been grabbed.

problems.problem: Jettison Fuel and weapon fire are winning the trade
problems.label: Mid Game
problems.when: Consider Metal Skin when fuel spray and weapon pressure are the part actually killing you. Activate for the committed bullet-damage window and move toward cover.
problems.how: Bullet immunity addresses weapon-damage pressure, but the fuel backblast, missile spirit damage and Close The Deal still need another response. It does not remove Bullet Resist reduction already applied.

problems.problem: One large spirit hit starts every losing fight
problems.label: Late Game
problems.when: Consider Spellbreaker when a large missile payoff or spirit impact leaves you unable to survive the rest of the fight. Compare Spirit Resilience if repeated smaller hits are the main problem.
problems.how: Conditional protection can soften a qualifying spirit burst. Its trigger and cooldown matter; it does not block the grab or guarantee protection against every hit of his multi-part abilities.

problems.problem: Abilities and active items keep rescuing him during your focus
problems.label: Late Game
problems.when: Choose Cursed Relic when the team has damage ready but Danny’s casts or active items keep denying the finish. Save the larger purchase for a coordinated catch.
problems.how: Use cast and item denial before his next defensive response or engage. It creates a focused damage window; it is not a promise to reverse a grab or remove an ultimate already in progress.

problems.problem: Slows and landing stuns leave you exposed too long
problems.label: Lane
problems.when: Buy Debuff Reducer when repeated slows or impact stuns make Danny’s follow-up difficult to escape. It is a smaller passive investment when losing movement time is the main problem.
problems.how: Debuff resistance shortens affected debuffs, including slow or stun pressure. Do not assume it shortens the entire Close The Deal flight sequence or reduces the damage itself.

problems.problem: His jetpack keeps denying your team a finish
problems.label: Lane
problems.when: Choose Slowing Hex when Danny’s jetpack movement lets him leave your damage or take another aerial angle. Have allies ready to use the catch rather than hexing from a position nobody can follow.
problems.how: Movement-skill silence restricts his jetpack mobility during the effect. Apply it before the movement you want to deny, and keep follow-up ready if he cleanses it. It is not an escape item for a player already caught in Close The Deal.

problems.problem: Fuel spray has reduced your Bullet Resist before the next exchange
problems.label: Mid Game
problems.when: Buy Dispel Magic when Jettison Fuel’s Bullet Resist reduction leaves you vulnerable to his weapon follow-up. Reset the debuff before taking another exposed trade.
problems.how: Clear the eligible fuel debuff, then leave the firing angle so he cannot immediately reapply it. The cleanse does not undo damage already taken, and it is not a way to remove Close The Deal’s ultimate grab.

problems.problem: Close The Deal catches you before you can press an active
problems.label: Late Game
problems.when: Consider Indomitable when Danny’s opening control repeatedly catches you before you can react. Check that its automatic protection is ready for the important engage.
problems.how: Its automatic response to qualifying control gives you protection against the opening catch without relying on a last-second button press. Earlier control can consume that response, and its barrier is not immunity to every part of Danny’s damage.

problems.problem: You need to keep acting through his grab or landing control
problems.label: Late Game
problems.when: Buy Unstoppable when Danny’s control threatens a planned engage or damage commitment. Activate before his grab or landing catches you, while you can still use the item.
problems.how: Crowd-control immunity protects your actions during its active window. It does not make you immune to missile, fuel or impact damage, and this recommendation depends on preparing the item before the control sequence.

problems.problem: His Spirit-scaling follow-up is forcing you out of lane
problems.label: Early / mid-game option
problems.when: Consider Spirit Sap when Danny’s Spirit-scaling ability damage is deciding trades and your team can pressure him with spirit damage.
problems.how: Apply before the next spell sequence while he is targetable. Keep leaving missile lines and respecting his landing or grab; this debuff does not remove marks, ground him or answer a separate weapon-damage build.

lane: Move out of Strix Salvo’s missile line before its delayed explosions. A mark makes the next charged shot more dangerous, so break the firing angle rather than extending the same trade.
Use bridges, doorways and overhead cover to limit his aerial shots. Keep stamina for leaving the missile line or a visible landing, rather than spending every dash on poke.
Leave Jettison Fuel’s spray instead of standing through weapon damage and Bullet Resist reduction. Its finishing backblast deals spirit damage, so bullet protection is not the whole answer.

Avoid Chimera Mk1’s landing blast. If he overheats and hits no hero, his self-stun creates a punish window while the jetpack cools. Jettison Fuel vents heat when it deals damage, so watch the actual landing and follow-up before chasing.
fight: Track his aerial approach without bunching up beneath it. Use overhead cover and reserve movement for the landing or close-range grab.
Use Knockdown on an exposed airborne Danny early enough for its delayed stun to land. Coordinate damage during the catch; do not treat the delay as an instant rescue after Close The Deal has started.
Land Silence Wave or Cursed Relic before his next cast when your team is ready to focus him. Denying the next engage is a different job from trying to cancel an ultimate that already grabbed someone.
Retreat earlier when low: Close The Deal deals extra damage to enemies below half health. Keep a teammate close enough to respond, while giving each other room to avoid the same landing explosion.
Respect his death explosion. After finishing him, move away from the body rather than standing over it at low health.

Prepare Unstoppable before the grab or landing control, or keep Indomitable’s automatic response available for the catch. Reactive Barrier protects follow-up after control; Dispel Magic is for eligible non-ultimate debuffs such as fuel resistance shred.

Deadman Danny is easier to punish when cover denies his aerial angle and he commits a landing without catching a hero. Move out of the missile line, avoid the overheat blast, and pressure him during the resulting self-stun or cooling window. Watch Jettison Fuel: dealing damage with it vents heat and can change his next movement window.

What should you buy first against Violet in lane?

Should you buy bullet or spirit defense against Violet?

Several abilities deal spirit damage, but Living Ink also increases bullet damage on its empowered shots. Start with the damage actually deciding your trades. Spirit protection is useful against ability pressure; a weapon-focused Violet can require a different defensive purchase.
How should you respond to Still Life?

Move toward solid cover to deny her sustained view instead of continuing an exposed damage trade. Still Life deals damage while Violet keeps the target in view, with extra damage and a stun when it completes.
Can you destroy Violet’s ink walls?

Yes. A heavy melee destroys a drawn stroke but deals spirit damage to you, so check your health and the enemy firing angle first. Her ultimate is a different effect, and the same method will not clear it.
What happens when you leave Abstract Landscape?

Leaving triggers spirit damage, silence and slow. Before its final upgrade the ink is destroyed in that process; after it, the ink persists. Do not count on a teleport avoiding the trigger or on casting an escape right after crossing.
Is anti-heal a priority against Violet?

Make it conditional on visible recovery. Healbane fits players who reliably apply spirit damage; Toxic Bullets fits reliable repeated weapon hits. Still Life can gain regeneration and Abstract Landscape can gain allied Spirit Lifesteal through upgrades. Buy anti-heal when that healing prevents a finish, not automatically at the start of every lane.
Does Dispel Magic remove Violet’s ultimate silence?
Do not rely on it for Abstract Landscape’s ultimate silence. Dispel Magic helps with eligible Flow State and Still Life effects; use it while you can still activate items.
Does Reactive Barrier help against Violet?
Yes, when qualifying control from Still Life or Abstract Landscape leads to lethal follow-up damage. The barrier helps you survive; it does not prevent the control or remove Violet’s ink.
Should you choose Debuff Reducer, Indomitable or Unstoppable?

Choose around the response you need. Debuff Reducer shortens eligible effects across exchanges, Indomitable responds automatically to qualifying control, and Unstoppable protects a planned commitment when activated in time. None of them answers every part of her kit.
Can Knockdown or silence cancel Still Life?
Knockdown offers a delayed catch, while Silence Wave can deny her next cast. Neither is a reliable way to stop an active Still Life, and neither removes ink already placed.

why: Reliable anti-heal for heroes that can consistently apply spirit damage
Offers a healing reward when an affected target is finished

best.note: His healing numbers are making fights drag forever
methods: Apply reliable anti-heal such as Healbane, Toxic Bullets, Decay, or Spirit Burn.
Rem can produce large healing totals, so healing reduction directly attacks the reason the fight is not ending.

best.note: Shiv keeps healing or stabilizing through extended fights
methods: Apply Healbane or another anti-heal source before the long trade.
Shiv gets far more value when fights drag on and he can recover around deferred damage, so healing reduction makes the eventual burst much more likely to stick.

best.note: Last Stand sustain is keeping him alive too long
methods: Apply anti-heal before the ultimate fight.
Warden's healing is not the only threat, but reducing it makes surviving and finishing the ultimate window much more realistic.

alts.text: Toxic Bullets gives weapon users anti-heal and percentage-health bleed after repeated shooting. It fits carries who can keep landing shots on a sustain target, with the application built before the enemy's important healing window.

Decay gives you a direct way to put healing reduction on a sustain target, alongside current-health damage over time. It suits fights where you need anti-heal applied deliberately before the enemy starts winning the health trade.

Spirit Burn rewards builds that can reach its spirit-damage trigger, adding an explosion, damage over time, and healing reduction. It combines damage scaling with anti-sustain pressure, but you must trigger the effect before the enemy's recovery decides the fight.

juggernaut.name: Громила
juggernaut.short: Reduces enemy fire rate when you take hits.
juggernaut.intro: Sustained rapid weapon pressure while you are being hit.
juggernaut.who: Frontline players repeatedly taking fire from opponents whose weapon pressure builds through sustained attacks.
juggernaut.when: Use it in the exchanges where enemy fire rate is the main reason you cannot hold space. Pair the purchase with a workable position rather than simply absorbing every shot.
juggernaut.watch: Reducing fire rate does not cleanse effects already applied or answer a spirit-heavy burst by itself.
juggernaut.buy: Buy it when repeated gunfire is wearing down your frontline and fire-rate reduction fits the way you fight. If you need to survive one short weapon burst, compare an immediate defensive active.

alts.text: Rusted Barrel reduces an enemy's fire rate, making sustained gun trades easier to manage. Apply it during the exchange you want to change, then use the reduced weapon pressure to contest the wave, reposition, or return damage.

Suppressor lets spirit-damage users reduce an enemy's fire rate through their damage pressure. It is useful when your spirit damage can reach a gun carry consistently, helping your team trade with less sustained weapon pressure.

Plated Armor offers passive chances to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects. Against repeated gun hits and stacking pressure, it can slow the buildup that makes the exchange dangerous, while leaving you free to manage positioning and other actives.

aprounds.name: Бронебой
aprounds.short: Bullet procs bypass barriers and bullet resistance.
aprounds.intro: Barrier-heavy or bullet-resistant targets, including Rat King using Royal Pestments.
aprounds.who: Weapon-focused heroes who can keep landing shots into bullet defense or barriers.
aprounds.when: Keep weapon pressure on the defended target so the proc has opportunities to contribute. Use a coordinated damage window rather than expecting a single shot to settle the fight.
aprounds.example: Against Rat King: Use Armor Piercer on a weapon carry or Cursed Relic if your team can commit a Tier 4 active. Armor Piercer can bypass Barriers, while Cursed Relic can strip non-ultimate barriers and buffs.
aprounds.watch: The bypass is described as a chance on bullets. Do not treat every shot as guaranteed barrier or resistance penetration.
aprounds.buy: Consider it once bullet defense or barriers are the main reason your weapon damage falls short. You still need reliable shooting access; a late damage investment cannot fix being unable to reach the target.
why: Keeps weapon pressure effective into heavy bullet defense

best.note: Rat King Royal Pestments barrier is making him impossible to finish
methods: Use Armor Piercer on a weapon carry or Cursed Relic if your team can commit a Tier 4 active.
Armor Piercer can bypass Barriers, while Cursed Relic can strip non-ultimate barriers and buffs.

alts.text: Bullet Resist Shredder makes a focused target more vulnerable to weapon damage. It shines when your own gun pressure and your teammates' bullets land together, turning a resistance reduction into a practical opening to finish the fight.

Tank Buster helps damage remain useful against large health pools through percentage current-health damage that bypasses spirit resistance. It addresses durability, while healing and defensive casts may still require separate answers from you or your team.

Cursed Relic creates a powerful team focus-fire window by interrupting, silencing, disarming, locking items, and removing non-ultimate buffs. Its outgoing-damage penalty makes allied follow-up central to the purchase: choose the target together and be ready to punish.

spellbreaker.name: Разрушитель чар
spellbreaker.short: Adds spirit defense and periodic protection against a large spirit hit.
spellbreaker.intro: Spirit burst and repeated debuff pressure, including the caster matchups linked below.
spellbreaker.who: Players who need stronger durability against spirit burst and the debuff pressure accompanying it.
spellbreaker.when: Use it for a fight decided by a large spirit hit and track whether its burst-protection effect is available. A smaller qualifying hit can spend that protection before the ability you wanted to survive.
spellbreaker.example: Against Apollo: Build Spellbreaker or Spirit Resilience. Apollo deals a large amount of front-loaded spirit damage, so spirit defense reduces the part of his combo that actually converts kills.
spellbreaker.watch: Spirit defense does not provide the same answer to a weapon-heavy build. Check the current damage source before committing your defensive budget.
spellbreaker.buy: Consider it when repeated spirit burst remains lethal despite your existing defenses. Choose it for the current damage source and watch the protection's availability before committing to a fight.
why: Helps survive a decisive spirit burst
Adds durability against ability damage and debuff pressure

best.note: His spirit burst is deleting you before you can trade back
methods: Build Spellbreaker or Spirit Resilience.
Apollo deals a large amount of front-loaded spirit damage, so spirit defense reduces the part of his combo that actually converts kills.

best.note: Celeste spirit burst is killing you before you can reach her
methods: Build Spellbreaker when the spell burst is the main problem.
It gives a much stronger spirit-defense layer than trying to chase her with only mobility items and helps you survive long enough to force her down.

best.note: Charge-shot spirit burst is putting you into execute range
methods: Build Spellbreaker or Spirit Resilience.
Late-game Talon damage often pivots toward spirit burst, and dedicated spirit defense reduces the single-hit spikes.

best.note: His spirit burst is chunking too much health at once
methods: Build Spellbreaker.
The item reduces the large spirit chunk and its debuff resistance also shortens several of the effects that make the follow-up lethal.

best.note: Vexing Bolt burst is deleting you from range
methods: Build Spellbreaker or Spirit Shielding.
His high-damage bolt pattern is spirit-heavy and can be reduced substantially with dedicated spirit defense.

alts.text: Spirit Resilience provides consistent passive protection against spirit damage. It helps when abilities keep wearing you down across multiple exchanges, giving you a baseline defense while you focus on positioning, cooldowns, and your own contribution to the fight.

Spirit Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of spirit damage, helping absorb what follows. It is useful when the opening ability hit starts a dangerous trade and a shield gives you time to reach cover or return manageable damage.

Debuff Reducer helps you spend less of each fight under status effects. It is a passive answer to repeated disruption, useful when shorter debuffs give you room to move or trade without relying on another active button.

veil-walker.name: Незримый покров
veil-walker.short: Uses veils for speed, stealth, and safer approaches.
veil-walker.intro: Long-range pressure and sniper angles that can be avoided with a safer rotation.
veil-walker.who: Players who can use veils as part of a safer rotation or approach route.
veil-walker.when: Choose a rotation through useful veil geometry and use the speed and stealth to change the enemy's ranged angle.
veil-walker.watch: Its route value depends on a useful veil. It does not give the same defense when you remain exposed in a direct damage exchange.
veil-walker.buy: Consider it when useful veil routes let you avoid ranged pressure or approach a fight from a better angle. Check the routes you actually use before buying for a situation where no veil is available.

alts.text: Warp Stone gives you an immediate position change and bullet resistance, helping escape a close threat or committed damage angle. Pick a destination that removes follow-up pressure; teleporting within the same danger wastes much of the opportunity.

Fleetfoot helps you manage fighting distance with an active speed boost. It suits heroes who want to keep pressure on a target while kiting away from close-range threats, or quickly change position before the next damaging exchange.

Enduring Speed helps you reclaim distance against slows and persistent chases. The speed and slow resistance matter most when they let you leave an enemy's preferred range, break an exposed angle, or arrive at cover before another trade.

siphon.name: Вытягивающие пули
siphon.short: Repeated hits temporarily steal a percentage of enemy maximum health.
siphon.intro: High-max-health targets, with Rat King as the direct recommendation.
siphon.who: Weapon users who can sustain hits on a large-health target through an extended fight.
siphon.when: Keep shooting during the useful health-swing window and coordinate the finish while the stolen health is still affecting the exchange.
siphon.example: Against Rat King: Use Siphon Bullets, Scourge, Toxic Bullets, Tank Buster, or Decay depending on your build. Health-steal, percentage-health damage, and anti-heal all scale well into a high-HP Rat King.
siphon.watch: The stolen health returns when the debuff expires. Treat the advantage as temporary rather than assuming the health reduction is permanent.
siphon.buy: Buy it when you can maintain weapon hits on a high-health opponent during longer fights. If their healing is the larger obstacle, make sure your team also has reliable anti-heal.
why: Creates a large temporary health swing during extended fights

best.note: His large health pool takes too long to burn down
methods: Use Siphon Bullets, Scourge, Toxic Bullets, Tank Buster, or Decay depending on your build.
Health-steal, percentage-health damage, and anti-heal all scale well into a high-HP Rat King.

alts.text: Tank Buster helps damage remain useful against large health pools through percentage current-health damage that bypasses spirit resistance. It addresses durability, while healing and defensive casts may still require separate answers from you or your team.

Scourge pairs defensive resistance with a close-range aura that damages enemies based on maximum health. It suits heroes who can stay near a large-health target without losing the fight simply to maintain aura uptime.

Toxic Bullets gives weapon users anti-heal and percentage-health bleed after repeated shooting. It fits carries who can keep landing shots on a sustain target, with the application built before the enemy's important healing window.

knockdown.name: Нокдаун
knockdown.short: Delayed stun for grounding flyers or interrupting vulnerable channels.
knockdown.intro: Aerial targets and vulnerable channels that your team can punish after the stun.
knockdown.who: Players who need to ground an aerial target or interrupt a vulnerable commitment with team follow-up.
knockdown.when: Account for the delay and cast while the target can still be affected. Against a channel, track whether protective immunity has already changed the interrupt opportunity.
knockdown.example: Against Bebop: Cast Knockdown while he is channeling in the air. The stun can interrupt the channel and the anti-air bonus makes airborne targets easier to punish.
knockdown.watch: The delayed stun is not an instant response. Protected channels and movement interactions need matchup-specific timing.
knockdown.buy: Buy it when a flying enemy or interruptible channel is repeatedly taking over fights. Confirm your team can follow up and that immunity will not protect the target when the delayed stun arrives.

best.note: His airborne ultimate is zoning the whole fight
methods: Cast Knockdown while he is channeling in the air.
The stun can interrupt the channel and the anti-air bonus makes airborne targets easier to punish.

best.note: She is staying airborne and impossible to finish
methods: Use Knockdown while she is elevated.
Forcing Celeste back to the floor removes the safe angle that lets her keep dealing damage while your team cannot reach her.

best.note: Dynamo is channeling Singularity without Unstoppable
methods: Use Knockdown as soon as the vulnerable channel begins.
The stun interrupts channeled abilities, so forcing Dynamo to buy or pre-use Unstoppable is valuable even when Knockdown is not a permanent answer.

best.note: He is sniping safely from the air in teamfights
methods: Use Knockdown while he is airborne.
The extended anti-air stun drops him into a position where your team can actually finish him.

best.note: She keeps split pushing and flying away
methods: Knockdown the flight.
Grounding Ivy cancels the safe escape angle and forces her to spend the cooldown without getting the rotation she wanted.

best.note: Ice Path lets him cast safely from above every fight
methods: Use Knockdown while Kelvin is airborne.
The anti-air control can force him through the path to the floor and remove the protected casting angle.

alts.text: Phantom Strike lets you commit directly to an enemy, ground them, and create a slowed, disarmed window. It can help punish an aerial carry, but the arrival point matters: your hero must survive where the target is standing.

Slowing Hex is a targeted answer to movement-dependent escapes. Use the slow and movement-skill silence before the relevant escape begins, with allies already in range to punish; a catch has little value if no one can finish the target.

Cursed Relic creates a powerful team focus-fire window by interrupting, silencing, disarming, locking items, and removing non-ultimate buffs. Its outgoing-damage penalty makes allied follow-up central to the purchase: choose the target together and be ready to punish.

unstoppable.name: Неудержимость
unstoppable.short: Proactive crowd-control immunity for an important commitment.
unstoppable.intro: Expected control chains and high-impact catches during a planned engage.
unstoppable.who: Players who can anticipate the engage and need protection through repeated control during a commitment.
unstoppable.when: Activate it proactively before entering the dangerous control window or before starting a commitment you need to complete.
unstoppable.example: Against Dynamo: Activate Unstoppable before the expected engage. Indomitable does not reliably free you from Singularity, while proactive CC immunity prevents the control from taking hold.
unstoppable.watch: It is a planned immunity window, not a reason to ignore positioning or damage. Save it for the control sequence that actually decides the fight.
unstoppable.buy: Buy it when your engage or damage window repeatedly fails because of control. It is especially useful when you can anticipate the fight and activate protection before losing the ability to act.

best.note: Singularity keeps catching you before you can react
methods: Activate Unstoppable before the expected engage.
Indomitable does not reliably free you from Singularity, while proactive CC immunity prevents the control from taking hold.

best.note: Repeated tornado lifts are controlling the entire fight
methods: Use Unstoppable for the multi-tornado control window.
The built-in debuff resistance and CC immunity are more reliable once he is repeatedly chaining tornado setups.

best.note: You are getting chained through several control effects
methods: Activate Unstoppable before the full engage.
When multiple effects are the problem, proactive immunity is more reliable than trying to purge each one individually.

best.note: A stolen ultimate is creating a fight-winning CC window
methods: Use Unstoppable when the copied ultimate is a major control threat.
Sinclair's danger changes by stolen ability, so flexible CC immunity is safer than buying for one specific copied spell.

best.note: Wraith Telekinesis is starting a kill combo
methods: Prepare Unstoppable for Telekinesis and activate it before control prevents the response, then leave the follow-up angle.
Telekinesis is an ultimate effect that Dispel Magic does not remove, and proactive immunity avoids relying on a narrow reaction window.

alts.text: Indomitable provides an automatic response to the next qualifying control effect, then adds a barrier and cooldown relief. It is valuable against catches that leave little time to press a defensive active, provided its protection is ready for the important event.

Counterspell rewards reading an enemy's commitment. By upgrading your parry to block ability damage and effects during its protection window, it lets you turn a predictable burst or control attempt into a missed opportunity for the opponent.

Debuff Reducer helps you spend less of each fight under status effects. It is a passive answer to repeated disruption, useful when shorter debuffs give you room to move or trade without relying on another active button.

counterspell.name: Контрчары
counterspell.short: Upgrades parry to block ability damage and effects.
counterspell.intro: Telegraphed burst or control sequences where you can read and react to the commitment.
counterspell.who: Players comfortable responding to a readable ability commitment with a prepared parry.
counterspell.when: Prepare the parry for the dangerous ability or damage window. The strongest use is blocking the part of the sequence that would otherwise decide the exchange.
counterspell.example: Against Apollo: Time Counterspell for the actual damage window of the ultimate. Correct timing can negate the ability damage and effects even after the sequence has started.
counterspell.watch: Using the response too early can waste the window. Sudden catches and repeated control may require a different defensive plan.
counterspell.buy: Buy it when a readable ability repeatedly decides your fights and you can react with parry. If the catch happens before you can respond, compare automatic control protection instead.

best.note: His ultimate is finishing you after the slow-motion setup
methods: Time Counterspell for the actual damage window of the ultimate.
Correct timing can negate the ability damage and effects even after the sequence has started.

best.note: His ultimate grab keeps converting into a kill
methods: Counterspell the pull or use Unstoppable/Ethereal Shift.
The ultimate is telegraphed enough to answer if you keep the defensive tool available.

best.note: His ultimate is about to land on you
methods: Preemptively Counterspell the obvious ultimate timing.
The animation is readable enough to protect yourself before the burst and effects connect.

best.note: His ultimate stun is deciding teamfights
methods: Counterspell the telegraphed explosion or Warp Stone out of range.
The wind-up gives you a real reaction window if you preserve the defensive tool.

best.note: Stone Form is stunning you for easy follow-up
methods: Counterspell the Stone Form impact.
The ability is telegraphed enough to parry, removing both the damage and the control that normally sets up the next hit.

best.note: She is low health but threatens a fight-winning health swap
methods: Counterspell the swap or silence her before she can cast it.
Chasing a low Geist is dangerous specifically because Soul Exchange can reverse the health bars instantly.

alts.text: Indomitable provides an automatic response to the next qualifying control effect, then adds a barrier and cooldown relief. It is valuable against catches that leave little time to press a defensive active, provided its protection is ready for the important event.

Unstoppable protects a planned commitment from crowd control. Activate it before the dangerous control sequence begins, especially when repeated disables would stop you from completing an engage or dealing damage. You still need a position that survives the incoming damage.

Ethereal Shift lets you sit out a dangerous moment through brief invulnerability and untargetability. Against a committed burst or a short ultimate window, the goal is to waste the enemy's investment and return with a plan for your next position.

divine-barrier.name: Божественный барьер
divine-barrier.short: Shields an ally and purges removable debuffs.
divine-barrier.intro: Burst and debuff setups where a teammate needs immediate protection.
divine-barrier.who: Players who need to protect an ally through burst or a removable debuff sequence.
divine-barrier.when: Keep an ally-save angle available and use the shield or cleanse when the threatened teammate can still benefit from the response.
divine-barrier.example: Against Bebop: Use Divine Barrier on the bombed teammate. It can cleanse removable non-stun debuffs from an ally, making it one of the best team-save answers when the bomb is on someone other than you.
divine-barrier.watch: An ally-save purchase needs attention to the teammate and their position. It does not remove the need to prevent the next catch or follow-up.
divine-barrier.buy: Consider it when a teammate is repeatedly targeted and an ally shield or cleanse would change the outcome. Choose a buyer who can watch that teammate and remain in position to use it.

best.note: A teammate is stuck with Bebop Sticky Bomb
methods: Use Divine Barrier on the bombed teammate.
It can cleanse removable non-stun debuffs from an ally, making it one of the best team-save answers when the bomb is on someone other than you.

best.note: Pocket Affliction is on a teammate and they need an immediate save
methods: Use Divine Barrier on the afflicted ally.
It can cleanse eligible negative effects from a teammate and is the team-oriented answer when Counterspell only protects the person who bought it.

alts.text: Rescue Beam combines healing with a positional teammate save. The pull can remove an ally from the enemy's ongoing damage angle, so a good rescue depends as much on where you bring them as on how much health they recover.

Dispel Magic resets a fight weighed down by removable non-ultimate debuffs. Use it to clear effects such as Bebop's Sticky Bomb before detonation, then reposition or recommit with the debuff gone. Its activation restrictions are part of the decision.

Reactive Barrier adds an automatic shield after a hard-control catch. It helps absorb the follow-up damage that often turns a stun into a kill, giving you a chance to reach cover or receive help once you can act again.

return-fire.name: Обратный огонь
return-fire.short: Reflects incoming damage during exchanges you can survive.
return-fire.intro: Sustained damage trades where opponents keep attacking into your defensive window.
return-fire.who: Durable brawlers who can survive incoming pressure and punish the opponent for continuing to hit them.
return-fire.when: Use it during a damage exchange you can survive, especially when sustained gun pressure makes reflection valuable.
return-fire.example: Against Silver: Use Return Fire during the sustained human-form weapon trade. Her rapid gun pattern can reflect meaningful damage back into her, especially on heroes that already have enough durability to stay in the exchange.
return-fire.watch: Reflected damage does not remove the incoming threat. Pair it with suitable defense and do not rely on it to win a damage race you cannot live through.
return-fire.buy: Buy it when you already have the durability to stay alive through incoming damage and reflection would punish sustained attacks. It is a follow-through purchase, not a replacement for the defense you need to survive.

best.note: Silver human-form gun pressure is punishing you before wolf form even starts
methods: Use Return Fire during the sustained human-form weapon trade.
Her rapid gun pattern can reflect meaningful damage back into her, especially on heroes that already have enough durability to stay in the exchange.

best.note: Her rapid-fire weapon pressure is melting you
methods: Use Return Fire if you are already durable, or Metal Skin if survival is the only goal.
Vyper fires enough shots to punish herself heavily into Return Fire, while Metal Skin simply blanks the bullets.

alts.text: Metal Skin gives you a temporary bullet-immunity window against decisive weapon pressure. Against a gun carry, activate it for the dangerous commitment and use that time to reach cover or let allies respond; it does not remove debuffs already on you.

Plated Armor offers passive chances to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects. Against repeated gun hits and stacking pressure, it can slow the buildup that makes the exchange dangerous, while leaving you free to manage positioning and other actives.

Disarming Hex stops a target from firing their weapon, creating breathing room against gun-focused carries. It is particularly useful when your team wants to keep fighting through the enemy's damage window rather than only protect one player.

weapon-shielding.name: Оружейная защита
weapon-shielding.short: Grants a barrier after a burst of weapon damage.
weapon-shielding.intro: Early weapon poke and gun-led lane pressure.
weapon-shielding.who: Laning players who need a shield response to repeated gun poke and want room to stabilize.
weapon-shielding.when: Use the shield window to take cover, improve spacing, or return a manageable trade before the next weapon exchange.
weapon-shielding.example: Against Drifter: Use a weapon-triggered barrier to stabilize the gun follow-up. A cleanse is a separate answer to the mark that enables the teleport.
weapon-shielding.watch: Weapon damage is the trigger; the resulting barrier can absorb other incoming damage too. If that trigger is unreliable in the matchup, compare a different defensive tool rather than assuming the barrier will always be available.
weapon-shielding.buy: Consider it when weapon poke repeatedly starts the enemy's winning trade and reliably triggers the barrier. If the lane is ability-led, compare Spirit Shielding or another defense suited to that damage.

best.note: His catch is followed by heavy weapon pressure
methods: Use a weapon-triggered barrier to stabilize the gun follow-up. A cleanse is a separate answer to the mark that enables the teleport.

alts.text: Plated Armor offers passive chances to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects. Against repeated gun hits and stacking pressure, it can slow the buildup that makes the exchange dangerous, while leaving you free to manage positioning and other actives.

Reactive Barrier adds an automatic shield after a hard-control catch. It helps absorb the follow-up damage that often turns a stun into a kill, giving you a chance to reach cover or receive help once you can act again.

Escalating Resilience rewards weapon users who can keep shooting through a longer exchange. Its bullet resistance builds as you attack, helping you hold your ground against sustained gun pressure while continuing to contribute damage.

spirit-sap.name: Спиритическое истощение
spirit-sap.short: Reduce one enemy’s Spirit Power and Spirit Resist.
spirit-sap.intro: These illustrate the targeted trade Spirit Sap can support. They are editorial examples, not a win-rate ranking or a claim that every build needs the item.
spirit-sap.who: Players who can safely target a threatening caster before the exchange, especially when their own hero or a teammate can follow up with spirit damage.
spirit-sap.when: Apply before the enemy’s next spell exchange, then use the affected target’s lower Spirit Resist. Keep a safe position; crossing an exposed firing lane just to apply the active can cost more than it gains.
spirit-sap.example: Against Baba: use Spirit Sap before a spell trade when her Spirit-scaling pressure is deciding the exchange. Coordinate allied spirit damage while she is affected, and keep a separate response for Threadsap, melee pressure or control.
spirit-sap.watch: Spirit Power reduction is not a flat reduction to all incoming damage. It does not silence, disarm, cleanse an effect on you or apply anti-heal. Do not assume it changes damage already applied, damage stored by a previous cast or existing summons without verifying the interaction.
spirit-sap.buy: Consider it early when a specific enemy’s Spirit-scaling damage is winning trades and your side can use the resistance reduction. Keep it useful in mid-game skirmishes by applying it immediately before coordinated pressure. It is less compelling when the decisive problem is weapon damage, an unavoidable catch, or a target your team cannot reach.
why: Weaken a target’s Spirit-scaling output before the next exchange
Help allied spirit damage against the same target

best.note: Her Spirit-scaling pressure is winning repeated trades
methods: Consider Spirit Sap when Threadsap-enhanced pressure or another Spirit-scaling part of Baba’s build is deciding the exchange.

Target Baba before the trade and return spirit damage while she is affected. It does not cleanse Threadsap, disarm her or stop Granny Long Legs; choose a separate answer when melee pressure or control is the main threat.

best.note: Charged Shot trades are costing you lane farm
methods: Consider Spirit Sap when Grey Talon’s Spirit-scaling shot damage is forcing you back and your side can trade with spirit damage.

Apply before his next shot window when you can target him safely, then return damage from cover. It does not block the shot, ground him or stop his ultimate; do not cross an exposed lane just to cast it.

best.note: His Spirit-scaling beam pressure is winning exchanges
methods: Consider Spirit Sap when Kelvin’s own spell damage is keeping you out of the fight and allied spirit damage can punish him.

Apply before the next connected exchange, then break the beam angle if it remains unsafe. Spirit Sap does not cancel the beam, remove the slow or replace anti-heal when recovery inside Frozen Shelter prevents a finish.

best.note: Her repeated Spirit-scaling pressure is costing you trades
methods: Consider Spirit Sap when Mina’s Spirit-scaling ability pressure is deciding the exchange and your team can return spirit damage.

Apply before the next trade while she is targetable. Keep a separate response for movement that denies your finish; Spirit Sap does not silence her escape or automatically answer weapon-focused damage.

best.note: Her Spirit-scaling pressure is winning your spell trades
methods: Consider Spirit Sap when Violet’s Spirit-scaling damage is deciding trades and your side can follow up with spirit damage.

Apply before the next exchange and attack from a covered angle. It does not cancel Still Life, remove drawn strokes or prevent Abstract Landscape’s exit effects. Keep a separate response when control rather than damage is deciding the fight.

alts.text: Grants a barrier after a burst of spirit damage.
Passive resistance against recurring spirit damage.
Adds spirit defense and periodic protection against a large spirit hit.
Silences enemies before an important escape or defensive cast.

containment.name: Замедляющие чары
containment.short: Slows the target and disables affected movement abilities.
containment.intro: Mobile targets whose escape depends on a movement skill affected by Slowing Hex.
containment.who: Players whose team can finish a target once a specific movement option is denied.
containment.when: Use it before the relevant movement skill and while allies can follow up. Against Kelvin, apply it before Ice Path; against Mina or Mirage, be ready to follow up after a cleanse.
containment.example: Against Apollo: Use Slowing Hex before he starts the movement sequence. It shuts off a large portion of Apollo's mobility and makes his commit much easier to punish.
containment.watch: It does not disable every movement tool, including The Doorman's Doorway. Movement that has already started may require a different response.
containment.buy: Buy it when a particular movement ability repeatedly lets an enemy dive and leave safely. Check that the ability is affected and prioritize the purchase before another uncontested escape.
why: Stop recasts of move tools like Apollo's 2

best.note: Apollo mobility and Flawless Advance keep letting him escape
methods: Use Slowing Hex before he starts the movement sequence.
It shuts off a large portion of Apollo's mobility and makes his commit much easier to punish.

best.note: Billy keeps using Rising Ram to disengage after every trade
methods: Apply Slowing Hex before or as Billy commits.
Denying the movement ability turns his normal hit-and-run pattern into a much riskier all-in and gives your team time to punish him.

best.note: She keeps diving and escaping before your team can finish her
methods: Apply Slowing Hex before the mobility chain.
Calico loses most of the movement tools that let her commit and leave safely.

best.note: She keeps chaining jump pads to escape or find barrel angles
methods: Apply Slowing Hex before she uses the jump pad.
It prevents the movement ability and removes the mobility that makes her so difficult to pin down.

best.note: Kelvin keeps starting Ice Path before your team can stop him
methods: Apply Slowing Hex before Ice Path is active.
The timing matters—using the anti-mobility item before he establishes the path is much more effective than trying to shut it down after he is already airborne.

best.note: He keeps escaping after starting fights
methods: Apply Slowing Hex after he commits.
Removing his movement options turns the dive from a safe hit-and-run into a punishable overextension.

alts.text: Knockdown gives your team a delayed stun to punish airborne targets and interrupt vulnerable channels. The delay is the key detail: cast while there is still time for the stun to land, and have damage ready when the target is controlled.

Capacitor combines weapon-build value with a targeted catch. Its projectile slows an enemy, prevents stamina usage, and restricts movement abilities and items, giving your team a window to punish a target that normally escapes.

Silence Wave creates a cast-denial window before an enemy uses an important ability. Land the projectile as your team is ready to commit, then punish while escape or defensive casts are restricted. A silence is not a universal answer to an already-running channel.

deflecting-armor.name: Латная броня
deflecting-armor.short: Chance to deflect bullets and prevent weapon on-hit effects.
deflecting-armor.intro: Extended weapon pressure and repeated gun-heavy trades.
deflecting-armor.who: Players facing repeated weapon hits and on-hit buildup who want passive protection rather than relying only on an active immunity window.
deflecting-armor.when: Choose it when repeated weapon on-hit buildup is deciding the exchange. Its chances to prevent on-hit application can slow the pressure from Haze, Infernus, or Mina before you reach the next dangerous trade.
deflecting-armor.example: Against Haze: Build Plated Armor for the extended weapon trade. Reducing her ability to build weapon pressure over time is more reliable than only blocking a short five-second window.
deflecting-armor.watch: Its on-hit prevention can also block spirit damage attached to Wraith’s Full Auto and Vindicta’s Flight shots. Separately cast cards, Assassinate and control effects still need their own response. Its protection is chance-based rather than a guaranteed immunity window. It also does not cleanse already-applied stacks; compare Metal Skin for immediate bullet immunity and Dispel Magic for removable accumulated debuffs.
deflecting-armor.buy: Buy it when recurring weapon hits and on-hit buildup are the problem across several fights. Compare Metal Skin for a deliberate immunity window and Dispel Magic for removable effects already applied.
why: Helps slow weapon on-hit buildup such as Haze’s Fixation
Useful against repeated weapon pressure and buildup-dependent builds
On-hit prevention also applies to spirit damage attached to Wraith’s Full Auto and Vindicta’s Flight shots; separate spells still need another answer.

best.note: Haze Fixation stacks and gun damage are snowballing
methods: Build Plated Armor for the extended weapon trade.
Reducing her ability to build weapon pressure over time is more reliable than only blocking a short five-second window.

best.note: Rapid gun pressure is building Afterburn too quickly
methods: Build Plated Armor or Juggernaut.
Reducing sustained weapon pressure slows down the buildup that enables the rest of his damage-over-time kit.

best.note: Card and weapon buildup are snowballing every trade
methods: Build Plated Armor when repeated weapon on-hit buildup is driving the trade.
Its chances to deflect bullets and prevent on-hit application can slow the pressure that supplies Wraith’s repeated weapon and card value.

best.note: Repeated weapon hits are building her passive pressure
methods: Use on-hit prevention to slow the buildup, and combine it with line-of-sight resets so the trade does not keep escalating.

alts.text: Metal Skin gives you a temporary bullet-immunity window against decisive weapon pressure. Against a gun carry, activate it for the dangerous commitment and use that time to reach cover or let allies respond; it does not remove debuffs already on you.

Weapon Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of weapon damage, helping absorb follow-up pressure. Use that shield window to reach cover or return a manageable trade instead of staying exposed until the next burst overwhelms you.

Escalating Resilience rewards weapon users who can keep shooting through a longer exchange. Its bullet resistance builds as you attack, helping you hold your ground against sustained gun pressure while continuing to contribute damage.

silence-glyph.name: Волна безмолвия
silence-glyph.short: Silences enemies before an important escape or defensive cast.
silence-glyph.intro: Ability-dependent targets whose next defensive or movement cast will decide the exchange.
silence-glyph.who: Players creating a team window before an enemy escape or defensive ability is cast.
silence-glyph.when: Land the silence before the important ability starts, then commit while the target's cast options are restricted.
silence-glyph.example: Against Apollo: Layer Silence Wave after his cleanse or when he commits. If Apollo removes the first movement lock, a silence creates a second shutdown window and prevents him from immediately chaining the abilities that let him escape.
silence-glyph.watch: Silence alone does not cancel a channel that has already started unless the source also interrupts. Use a interrupt when that is the required job.
silence-glyph.buy: Buy it when an escape or defensive ability keeps denying a kill and a direct silence would let your team finish. For a channel that has already begun, check whether you need an interrupt instead.

best.note: Apollo cleanses Slowing Hex and escapes anyway
methods: Layer Silence Wave after his cleanse or when he commits.
If Apollo removes the first movement lock, a silence creates a second shutdown window and prevents him from immediately chaining the abilities that let him escape.

best.note: Lady Geist health swap is too hard to Counterspell on reaction
methods: Silence Wave her before she reaches the swap window.
Preventing the ultimate from being cast is more reliable than trying to react perfectly once a low-health Geist is already in range.

best.note: She keeps cleansing the first movement lock and escaping
methods: Layer a second control source such as Silence Wave or Cursed Relic.
Mina commonly has a cleanse answer, so one isolated Slowing Hex may not be enough in an important fight.

best.note: Paige keeps casting Plot Armor or defensive utility before the burst lands
methods: Silence Wave before your team commits damage.
Preventing the defensive spell is often more efficient than trying to chew through the barrier after Paige has already stabilized the trade.

best.note: Briefcase keeps waiting out your kill window
methods: Silence Pocket before committing the movement lock.
Preventing Briefcase stops Pocket from hiding through the duration of your control and then escaping afterward.

best.note: Doorway is letting him escape or re-enter fights for free
methods: Silence him before the Doorway cast.
Doorway is not treated as a movement ability, so Slowing Hex is not the answer; ability silence is.

alts.text: Cursed Relic creates a powerful team focus-fire window by interrupting, silencing, disarming, locking items, and removing non-ultimate buffs. Its outgoing-damage penalty makes allied follow-up central to the purchase: choose the target together and be ready to punish.

Silencer turns sustained weapon hits into pressure against ability-reliant enemies, reducing outgoing spirit damage and building toward silence. It fits gun users who can stay on a target long enough to restrict the cast that would otherwise turn the fight.

Slowing Hex is a targeted answer to movement-dependent escapes. Use the slow and movement-skill silence before the relevant escape begins, with allies already in range to punish; a catch has little value if no one can finish the target.

discord.name: Кара
discord.short: Adds resistance and a close-range maximum-health damage aura.
discord.intro: High-health targets you can pressure at close range; Rat King is the direct recommendation.
discord.who: Close-range players who can remain near a high-health enemy long enough to use the aura.
discord.when: Use its durability and aura during a close fight you can safely maintain. The percentage-health damage has a clear purpose against a large health pool.
discord.watch: The aura needs proximity. Chasing into an unsafe area for uptime can cost more than the purchase contributes.
discord.buy: Consider it when a high-health enemy is difficult to finish and your hero naturally fights nearby. Make sure your build can hold that distance safely before investing in an aura that needs proximity.
why: Percentage-health damage punishes huge health pools
Adds durability while you stay close enough to pressure

alts.text: Siphon Bullets creates a temporary health swing through repeated weapon hits, stealing a percentage of the enemy's maximum health. Against a large-health target, sustained contact and a coordinated finish help convert that temporary advantage before the stolen health returns.

Tank Buster helps damage remain useful against large health pools through percentage current-health damage that bypasses spirit resistance. It addresses durability, while healing and defensive casts may still require separate answers from you or your team.

Decay gives you a direct way to put healing reduction on a sustain target, alongside current-health damage over time. It suits fights where you need anti-heal applied deliberately before the enemy starts winning the health trade.

health-stimpak.name: Обряд лечения
health-stimpak.short: Recovers health during a safe window between fights.
health-stimpak.intro: Lane attrition where a safe reset can restore useful farming time.
health-stimpak.who: Laning players who have a safe recovery opportunity and need health back before returning to farm.
health-stimpak.when: Find a safe window for the channel, recover, then return from a position that reduces the next poke exchange.
health-stimpak.watch: A channelled recovery tool needs a usable window. It is not an immediate answer to the burst that is already killing you.
health-stimpak.buy: Buy it during a difficult lane when you have safe recovery windows but cannot afford to keep leaving farm. It will not solve a burst that kills you before you can get out.

alts.text: Extra Regen is a lane-stabilizing purchase for health lost between trades. The value comes from staying available to last-hit and contest souls: recover behind cover, adjust your angle, and avoid giving back the same health to free poke.

Restorative Locket turns accumulated stacks into a self-heal, helping you stay present through repeated exchanges. The reset is most useful when it gives you enough health to keep farming or rejoin a fight from a better angle.

Spirit Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of spirit damage, helping absorb what follows. It is useful when the opening ability hit starts a dangerous trade and a shield gives you time to reach cover or return manageable damage.

vex-barrier.name: Барьерная реакция
vex-barrier.short: Automatically grants a shield after a hard-control catch.
vex-barrier.intro: Hooks, charges, and other control-led lane combos.
vex-barrier.who: Laning players who need automatic durability when a hard-control catch starts the enemy combo.
vex-barrier.when: Use the triggered shield as a survival window after the catch. Move to a better angle or let a teammate cover the follow-up.
vex-barrier.example: Against Abrams: Buy Reactive Barrier as an early lane stabilizer. Shoulder Charge and other movement-lock effects trigger the barrier and restore stamina, giving you enough protection to survive the immediate melee follow-up.
vex-barrier.watch: A shield after control is not the same as preventing the control. It may stabilize a catch without stopping the rest of a repeated sequence.
vex-barrier.buy: Consider it when you survive the catch itself but die to the damage that follows. Its shield helps you endure the combo; choose control prevention if losing your actions is the main problem.
why: Adds a barrier after a qualifying hard-control hit
Useful when surviving the first catch gives you time to respond; it does not remove the control

best.note: Abrams Shoulder Charge combo is bursting you in lane
methods: Buy Reactive Barrier as an early lane stabilizer.
Shoulder Charge and other movement-lock effects trigger the barrier and restore stamina, giving you enough protection to survive the immediate melee follow-up.

best.note: Ivy Stone Form stun keeps starting lane kill attempts
methods: Buy Reactive Barrier if Stone Form is repeatedly starting the combo.
The automatic barrier and stamina restore give you immediate protection after the stun and are much cheaper than committing to a late-game anti-CC item.

alts.text: Indomitable provides an automatic response to the next qualifying control effect, then adds a barrier and cooldown relief. It is valuable against catches that leave little time to press a defensive active, provided its protection is ready for the important event.

Unstoppable protects a planned commitment from crowd control. Activate it before the dangerous control sequence begins, especially when repeated disables would stop you from completing an engage or dealing damage. You still need a position that survives the incoming damage.

Spirit Shielding creates a barrier after a burst of spirit damage, helping absorb what follows. It is useful when the opening ability hit starts a dangerous trade and a shield gives you time to reach cover or return manageable damage.

rupture.name: Разложение
rupture.short: Targeted healing reduction with current-health damage over time.
rupture.intro: High-health sustain targets and fights where healing is preventing a finish.
rupture.who: Players who want a direct anti-heal application without needing repeated weapon buildup.
rupture.when: Apply it before committing into the target's sustain. Keep the fight focused during the damage-over-time and healing-reduction window.
rupture.example: Against Lady Geist: Apply Decay before the finish attempt. Strong healing reduction plus current-health damage attacks the exact sustain window she relies on to survive while low.
rupture.watch: Owning anti-heal is not enough if the application comes after the healing trade has already turned the fight. It also does not replace distance or control.
rupture.buy: Buy it when healing is extending fights and your build cannot reliably apply another anti-heal option. Make the purchase before the next sustain-heavy engagement and use it as your team commits.
why: Long-duration anti-heal that does not need repeated weapon buildup

best.note: Her health and sustain build keeps surviving our damage
